mainTopic: What 'מועדי ה׳' excludes (שבת and הפרת נדרים), and why ט״ו באב was a day of great joy
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא saying that 'מועדי ה׳' were stated but שבת בראשית (or, according to בן עזאי, הפרת נדרים) 'was not stated', even though both appear in the Torah. רבי יוסי בר נתן could not understand it, so he traveled to find רב ששת. רב ששת explained that these topics do not share a special rule of the מועדים: שבת needs no קידוש בית דין, and הפרת נדרים needs no מומחין. The גמרא challenges this from 'ראשי המטות' and answers that the פסוק teaches that even a single expert can release a vow. Then a new topic begins with a משנה: ט״ו באב and יום הכפורים were the most joyous days for ישראל. The גמרא asks what made ט״ו באב special. שמואל says the שבטים were allowed to marry each other, and רבי יוחנן says שבט בנימין was allowed back in. רב נחמן says it was the day the מתי מדבר stopped dying, and the supporting teaching continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא: Festivals were stated, Shabbat and vow-annulment were not
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that 'מועדי ה׳' were stated, but שבת בראשית was not. בן עזאי says 'מועדי ה׳' were stated, but הפרת נדרים was not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Festivals of ה׳ were stated, but the Shabbat of Creation was not stated. בן עזאי says: The Festivals of ה׳ were stated, but the annulment of vows was not stated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it began quoting just before. The ברייתא contains two short, mysterious statements about what the phrase 'מועדי ה׳' includes and what it leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both statements use the same pattern: 'the מועדים were said, but X was not said.' Taken literally, this makes no sense, because שבת and הפרת נדרים are both written in the Torah right near the מועדים. The rest of the section explains what these statements really mean.

keyTerms.meaning: The Festivals of ה׳ (the יום טוב days)
The weekly שבת, which remembers Creation
Annulling or releasing vows
Were stated or said

steps.confusionAlert: 'Was not stated' does NOT mean the Torah never mentions שבת or הפרת נדרים. Both do appear in the Torah. The ברייתא means something else, and רב ששת explains it in steps 3 and 5.

phrases.english: The Festivals of the Lord were stated,
but the Shabbat of Creation was not stated.
Ben Azzai says:
The Festivals of the Lord were stated,
but the annulment of vows was not stated.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוֹעֲדֵי ה׳ נֶאֶמְרוּ, שַׁבַּת בְּרֵאשִׁית לֹא נֶאֶמְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that the earlier part of the sugya began quoting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Something special applies to the מועדים that does not apply to שבת בראשית (first opinion) or to הפרת נדרים (בן עזאי).

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר נתן travels to ask רב ששת what the ברייתא means
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר נתן knew this ברייתא but could not explain it. He looked for רב ששת in נהרדעא, then found him in מחוזא, and asked what 'שבת בראשית was not stated' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר נתן had learned this ברייתא but did not know how to explain it. He went after רב ששת to נהרדעא and did not find him. He went after him to מחוזא and found him. He asked him: What does 'The Festivals of ה׳ were stated, but Shabbat of Creation was not stated' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: A short story sets up the explanation. A scholar who is stuck on this ברייתא travels to find רב ששת and asks him what the first statement means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is real: שבת is written at the very start of the Torah's section on the מועדים, so how can the ברייתא say it 'was not stated'? The story shows how hard the line was, and it gets us ready for רב ששת's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: He had learned it (knew it by heart)
A ברייתא (here, the teaching just quoted)
To explain it
He went after him (went looking for him)
He found him

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר נָתָן גְּמִיר לַהּ לְהָא מַתְנִיתָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Natan had learned this baraita,
but did not know how to explain it.
He went after Rav Sheshet to Neharde'a,
but did not find him.
He went after him to Mechoza, and found him.
He said to him: What is meant by
"The Festivals of the Lord were stated,
but the Shabbat of Creation was not stated"?
phrases.notes: This is puzzling because שבת is written right inside the Torah's section on the Festivals, in ויקרא 23:3.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the first statement of the ברייתא in step 1 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does it mean that שבת בראשית 'was not stated', when שבת is written alongside the מועדים?

steps.title: רב ששת: Festivals need the court to sanctify them, Shabbat does not
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the מועדים depend on קידוש בית דין, but שבת does not. The ברייתא needed to say this because, since שבת is written next to the מועדים, we might have thought it also needs the court.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The Festivals of ה׳ need sanctification by the בית דין. The Shabbat of Creation does not need sanctification by the בית דין. You might have thought: since שבת is written next to the Festivals, it should need sanctification by the בית דין like the Festivals. So the ברייתא teaches us that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question. 'Was not stated' means the special rule of the מועדים, that the בית דין must sanctify them, was not said about שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dates of the מועדים depend on when the בית דין declares the new month, so the court is involved in setting them. שבת comes every seventh day by itself, with no court needed. The ברייתא had to say this because שבת appears in the same section as the מועדים, so we might have linked their rules together.

keyTerms.meaning: Sanctification (fixing the date) by the court
It might have entered your mind to say (what you might have wrongly thought)
Since they are written next to
It teaches us (that the wrong idea is not true)

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer shows how to read the ברייתא's pattern. 'X was not stated' means X does not share the special rule of the מועדים. רב ששת uses the same pattern for בן עזאי's line in the next steps.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מוֹעֲדֵי ה׳ צְרִיכִין קִידּוּשׁ בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.english: He said to him: The Festivals of the Lord require sanctification by the court,

phrases.aramaic: שַׁבַּת בְּרֵאשִׁית אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה קִידּוּשׁ בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: but the Shabbat of Creation does not require sanctification by the court.
It might enter your mind to say:
since it is written next to the Festivals,
it should require sanctification by the court like the Festivals;
so it teaches us that it does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מוֹעֲדֵי ה׳ צְרִיכִין קִידּוּשׁ בֵּית דִּין
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Not stated' means שבת does not need קידוש בית דין, unlike the מועדים. The ברייתא says this to block the idea that being written next to them makes שבת follow their rule.

steps.title: What does בן עזאי's statement about vows mean?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר נתן now asks about the second line: what does 'הפרת נדרים was not stated' mean?
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'The Festivals of ה׳ were stated, but the annulment of vows was not stated' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner moves on to בן עזאי's statement and asks the same kind of question about it. This sets up רב ששת's second answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, the Torah does discuss הפרת נדרים, right after the section on the מועדים. So 'was not stated' cannot mean it is missing from the Torah, and the meaning needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: What (does this mean)?

phrases.english: What is meant by "The Festivals of the Lord were stated,
but the annulment of vows was not stated"?
phrases.notes: The Torah's section on vows comes right after the Festivals, in במדבר 30.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״מוֹעֲדֵי ה׳ נֶאֶמְרוּ, הֲפָרַת נְדָרִים לֹא נֶאֶמְרָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first statement was explained, the questioner turns to the second statement of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What rule of the מועדים does בן עזאי say does not apply to הפרת נדרים?

steps.title: Festivals need expert judges, annulling vows does not
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the מועדים need מומחין (expert judges), but הפרת נדרים does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Festivals of ה׳ need experts. The annulment of vows does not need experts.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers using the same pattern as before. The special rule here is that the מועדים need מומחין, and that rule does not carry over to הפרת נדרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting the months and the מועדים has to be done by מומחין, judges who are true experts. Even though הפרת נדרים is written right next to the מועדים, it does not share this requirement. So both lines of the ברייתא have the same structure: a nearby topic does not take on a special rule of the מועדים.

keyTerms.meaning: Experts (fully qualified judges)
They require (need)

steps.whatToRemember: The phrase 'מועדי ה׳ נאמרו, X לא נאמר' means X does not share a special rule of the מועדים. For שבת בראשית, that rule is קידוש בית דין. For הפרת נדרים, it is the need for מומחין. Being written next to the מועדים does not mean having the same rules.

phrases.english: The Festivals of the Lord require experts,
phrases.notes: The answer comes without 'he said to him,' but it is still רב ששת answering.

phrases.english: but the annulment of vows does not require experts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 4, using the same pattern as the answer in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Not stated' means הפרת נדרים does not need מומחין, unlike the מועדים.

steps.title: But the Torah says 'heads of the tribes'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת: the section about vows opens with 'ראשי המטות', which suggests leaders or experts are needed for הפרת נדרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written 'the heads of the tribes'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks what רב ששת just said, that הפרת נדרים does not need experts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section of the Torah about vows begins by speaking to 'ראשי המטות', the heads of the tribes. That sounds like releasing vows belongs to important, expert people. So how can רב ששת say experts are not needed?

keyTerms.meaning: The heads of the tribes (the opening words of the Torah's section on vows)
But it is written! (a formula for a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: But it is written: "The heads of the tribes"!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that הפרת נדרים does not need מומחין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק addresses vows to 'ראשי המטות', which implies that experts or leaders are required.

steps.title: One expert alone is enough
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא in the name of רבי יוחנן answers that 'ראשי המטות' teaches that a single expert can release vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It is done by a single expert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The פסוק is not asking for a full court of experts. It teaches that one expert by himself can release a vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת said הפרת נדרים does not need מומחין at all; ordinary people can do it. 'ראשי המטות' is not a requirement for experts. It teaches an extra option: one expert can release a vow by himself. So the פסוק does not contradict רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: A single expert (one qualified judge acting alone)

steps.whatToRemember: The מועדים need a court of experts. הפרת נדרים does not need such a court, and even one expert alone can do it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
By a single expert.
phrases.notes: So 'heads of the tribes' teaches that one expert can release a vow all by himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בְּיָחִיד מוּמְחֶה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ראשי המטות' means a court of experts is needed, the same as for the מועדים
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ראשי המטות' teaches that a single expert can release vows, so there is no need for a court of experts

steps.title: The most joyous days: ט״ו באב and יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in which רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says ט״ו באב and יום הכפורים were the happiest days for ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there in a משנה: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said, there were no days as joyous for ישראל as the fifteenth of Av and יום הכפורים. On these days the daughters of ירושלים would go out in borrowed white clothes, so as not to embarrass a girl who had none of her own.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts here. The גמרא brings a משנה from another מסכת to set up a question about ט״ו באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה puts ט״ו באב on the same level of joy as יום הכפורים. Everyone wore borrowed white clothes, so a poor girl would not stand out. The next step will ask why ט״ו באב deserves such joy.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there (in a משנה from another מסכת)
The fifteenth day of the month of Av
Borrowed white garments
So as not to embarrass

phrases.english: We learned there:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
There were no days as joyous for Israel
as the fifteenth of Av and as Yom Kippur,
for on them the daughters of Jerusalem would go out
in borrowed white garments,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לְבַיֵּישׁ אֶת מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ.
phrases.english: so as not to embarrass one who did not have her own.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם, אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, connected to the theme of marriage between the שבטים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ט״ו באב and יום הכפורים were the most joyous days for ישראל

steps.title: Why is ט״ו באב so joyous?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands why יום הכפורים is joyous, but asks what is special about ט״ו באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for יום הכפורים: it is a day of pardon and forgiveness, and the day the second לוחות were given. But the fifteenth of Av, what is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to understand the משנה. It is setting up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יום הכפורים has clear reasons for joy: forgiveness, and receiving the second לוחות. ט״ו באב has no obvious reason, so the גמרא asks what happened on that day.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (one part is understood, another is not)
Pardon and forgiveness
The second (last) tablets

phrases.english: Granted, Yom Kippur:
it is a day of pardon and forgiveness,
the day on which the last Tablets were given.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב – מַאי הִיא?
phrases.english: But the fifteenth of Av, what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind part of the משנה in step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What event made ט״ו באב a day of great joy

steps.title: שמואל: the day the tribes could marry each other
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל says ט״ו באב was the day the שבטים were allowed to marry into one another. The limit in 'זה הדבר' was only for that one generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: It was the day the tribes were permitted to marry one another. What did they learn from? 'This is the matter': this matter applies only in this generation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer. ט״ו באב is the day when marriage between different שבטים was allowed again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah had told the daughters who inherit land to marry only within their own שבט, so the land would not move from one tribe to another. The words 'זה הדבר' were read as 'this matter is only for this generation'. Once that generation passed, the limit ended, and that was a reason for joy.

keyTerms.meaning: To 'enter' one another, meaning to marry between tribes
What did they explain (from which פסוק did they learn this)?
'This is the matter' (במדבר 36:6)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
It was the day the tribes were permitted
to enter into one another.
phrases.notes: That is, marry someone from a different tribe.

phrases.english: What did they interpret?
"This is the matter":
this matter shall not apply
except in this generation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: יוֹם שֶׁהוּתְּרוּ שְׁבָטִים לָבֹא זֶה בָּזֶה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ט״ו באב was the day marriage between the tribes was allowed again, because 'זה הדבר' limited the rule to one generation

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the day שבט בנימין was let back in
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן gives a different answer. ט״ו באב was the day שבט בנימין was allowed to marry into ישראל again, because the oath said 'ממנו', meaning only us and not our children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It was the day שבט בנימין was permitted to enter the congregation, as it says: 'The men of ישראל swore at מצפה, saying: None of us shall give his daughter to בנימין as a wife.' What did they learn from? 'Of us', and not of our children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the question about ט״ו באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the war with בנימין, the other tribes swore not to give their daughters to men of בנימין. They later noticed the oath said 'ממנו', 'none of us'. So it covered only the people who swore, not their children. When that was understood, בנימין could marry into the other tribes again, and that day was ט״ו באב.

keyTerms.meaning: To enter the congregation (to be allowed to marry into ישראל)
Swore at מצפה
'Of us', and not 'of our children'

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers for ט״ו באב: שמואל says the tribes were allowed to marry each other, and רבי יוחנן says שבט בנימין was allowed back in. Both answers learn from a פסוק that the limit was only for one generation.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
It was the day the tribe of Binyamin was permitted
to enter the congregation,
as it is written:
"And the men of Israel swore in Mitzpah, saying:
None of us shall give his daughter
to Binyamin as a wife."
What did they interpret?
"Of us," and not of our children.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: יוֹם שֶׁהוּתַּר שֵׁבֶט בִּנְיָמִן לָבֹא בַּקָּהָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the question of step 9, different from שמואל's answer
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ט״ו באב was the day שבט בנימין was allowed back into marriage, because the oath at Mitzpah bound only the people who swore, not their children

steps.title: Third answer: the day the wilderness deaths ended
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי בר יוסף, quoting רב נחמן, says ט״ו באב was the day the מתי מדבר stopped dying. The גמרא then begins a supporting source with 'דאמר מר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי בר יוסף said in the name of רב נחמן: ט״ו באב was the day when the people who were meant to die in the מדבר stopped dying. As the Master said: as long as the מתי מדבר had not yet stopped dying...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer to why ט״ו באב was a happy day: it was the day the dying of the מדבר generation came to an end. It then starts quoting a source to support this, and that quote continues in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two answers were about marriage: the שבטים marrying each other, and שבט בנימין being allowed back in. This answer is a completely different kind of reason. The joy is that a long punishment of death finally stopped. The words 'דאמר מר' show that רב נחמן is relying on a known teaching, which the גמרא is about to quote in full.

keyTerms.meaning: The dead of the wilderness: the generation that left מצרים and was sentenced to die in the מדבר
Ended, finished, came to a stop

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the story ends here. The sentence 'עד שלא כלו מתי מדבר' is only the start of a quote, and the גמרא finishes it in the next lines.

phrases.aramaic: רַב דִּימִי בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Dimi bar Yosef said that Rav Naḥman said:
It was the day on which the dead of the wilderness came to an end;
phrases.notes: That's the generation sentenced to die in the מדבר after the sin of the spies (במדבר 14:29–30).

phrases.english: As the Master said:
As long as the dead of the wilderness had not yet come to an end,

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: ראיה (for the 'דאמר מר' part that introduces a supporting source)
steps.triggerLanguage: רַב דִּימִי בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: יוֹם שֶׁכָּלוּ בּוֹ מֵתֵי מִדְבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third, different answer to the question in Step 9, alongside the answers of Steps 10 and 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What made ט״ו באב a day of joy (asked in Step 9).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ט״ו באב was the day the מתי מדבר stopped dying, backed up by a teaching introduced with 'דאמר מר'.
